1.  This appeal arises out of award dated 26.02.2016 passed by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kunkuri, District Jashpur (C.G.) in M.A.C.T. No.15/2012 awarding compensation of Rs.37,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of application till its realization, in favour of the appellant/claimant.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The claim of appellant/claimant before the Tribunal, in brief, was that on 27.08.2008, while claimant Gokaran Dansena after leaving his child at school was going to Pathalgaon Court,
respondent No.1-Satyaram Chauhan driving the offending bus bearing registration No.CG 13 A 2037 hit him near FCI Godown, as a result of which, he suffered grievous injuries on his head.

The appellant was first treated at Pathalgaon and then at District Hospital, Raigarh and thereafter,
considering the nature of injury, he was referred to Raipur where he was admitted and treated in M.M.I hospital, Raipur.

Upon report being made in this regard, crime was registered against Gokaran Dansena vs Satyaram Chauhan on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6392433/
1 respondent no.1 (Driver of the offending vehicle) at PS Pathalgaon, District Jashpur.
3.
It was claimed by Claimant Gokaran that before accident, he was earning Rs.12,000/- per month from the profession of advocacy.

On account of the accident, he received grievous injuries on his head, for which, he was admitted and treated in M.M.I hospital, Raipur where the tear duct of his eye was operated by Dr. Rakesh Gupta and the treatment is still going on.

Therefore, the claimant preferred an application before the Claims Tribunal claiming total compensation of Rs.16,70,000/-
for disability, loss in future income, physical and mental agony, medical expenses and also under other heads.

4. Learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents brought on record, awarded Rs.10,000 for pain and suffering, Rs.15,000 for loss of income during treatment, Rs.3,000 for Assistant, Rs.1000 for nutritious diet, Rs.3,000 for medical expenses and Rs.5,000 for loss of amenities in life.
Accordingly, the Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.37,000 in favour of the claimant with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of application till its realization.
While passing the impugned award, the Tribunal has exonerated the insurance company from its liability on the ground of breach of policy conditions.
Hence, this appeal is for enhancement and for an order of pay and recover.

5. Learned counsel for appellant/claimant submits that the Claims Tribunal has failed to consider the nature of injuries suffered by the appellant and awarded a total compensation of Rs.37,000 which is a very small amount and needs to be enhanced.
He submits that the Tribunal has not considered the medical bills Ex.P-13 to P-111 and has awarded only Rs.3,000 towards medical expenses which needs to be recomputed.
He further submits that though the insurance company has been exonerated, considering the beneficiary legislation of the Motor Vehicles Act, an order of pay and recovery may be passed.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondents oppose the submission made by the counsel for appellant and submit that in the facts and circumstances of case, the award passed by the Claims Tribunal is proper and requires no further enhancement.
Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company also opposes the prayer for issuance of an order of pay and recover.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.
In a motor accident claim case, what is important is that, the compensation to be awarded by the Courts/Tribunals should be just and proper compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It should neither be a meager amount of compensation, nor a Bonanza.
9. Now this Court shall examine as to whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper compensation in the given facts and circumstances of the case.
10. Only Rs.3,000/- has been given for medical expenses.
The appellant has presented medical documents and bills i.e. Exhibits P-13 to P-111 which are said to be Rs.1,69,755/- in total.

2
Tribunal has refused to grant the said amount on the ground that no authorized person has appeared for evidence to certify the doctor's prescription in respect of the same.
The discharge ticket (Ex.P-10), test reports, Out Patent Unit Cards (Ex.P-148 and P-149) etc. of MMI Hospital are attached with the record.
Keeping them in view, the medical bills presented do not appear to be fabricated and perusal of the same reveals that the appellant was admitted and treated in the said hospital for about 18 days.

11. In the above situation, as per Para-12 of the award of the Tribunal, the amount of Rs.3,000/-
calculated towards medical expenses is enhanced to Rs.1,70,000/-.
The amount awarded for pain and suffering and also for loss of income during treatment is kept as it is.
However, the amount awarded towards Assistant is enhanced from Rs.3,000/- to Rs.5,000 and the amount given for Nutritious Diet is enhanced from Rs.1,000/- to Rs. 5,000/-.
The amount awarded for loss of amenities in life is kept unchanged.

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant would become entitled for total compensation in the following manner:-
 Heads Compensation Modified/
 awarded by enhanced  Tribunal amount  Pain & suffering 10,000 10,000  Loss of income during treatment 15,000 15,000  Assistant 3,000 5,000  Nutritious diet 1,000 5,000  Medical expenses 3,000 1,70,000  loss of amenities in life 5,000 5,000
Total compensation Rs. 2,10,000 12.

Thus, the total compensation is recomputed as Rs.2,10,000 from which after deduction of Rs.37,000 as awarded by the Tribunal, the enhanced compensation would be Rs.1,73,000.
13.
So far as the prayer for issuing an order of "pay and recover" is concerned, the Tribunal has exonerated the insurance company considering that there is a breach of policy condition.
The claimant/appellant requested for an order for Pay & Recover.
On which, both the parties were heard.
14. In the present case, admittedly, the offending vehicle was insured with respondent no.3 but due to breach of policy condition, the insurance company has been exonerated.
However, considering the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh & another.

Vs. Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited & others reported in (2018) 7 SCC 558 ordering the insurance company to pay first and then recover and also taking note of the facts and circumstances of the present case, particularly the fact that at the time of accident the vehicle was insured with insurance company

In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
The appellant/claimant shall be entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,73,000 in addition to what is already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of enhancement of the award till its realization.
Accordingly, the impugned award stands modified to the above extent and rest of the conditions shall remain intact.
16. The Registry is directed to communicate the claimant in writing "the enhanced amount" in this appeal as against the award made by the Claims Tribunal.

The said communication be made in Hindi (Deonagri) language and the help of paralegal workers may be availed with a co-ordination of Secretary, Legal Aid of the concerned area wherein the claimant resides.
